Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:1.hebrew: ונהגו בני כופרא - בעלי ספינה קרי בני כופרא, לפי שזופתין אותם בזפת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:1.english: And the men of pitch [benei kufera] are accustomed - [The Gemara] calls shipowners benei kufera, because they coat them [the ships] with pitch.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:2.hebrew: אגרא בשעת משיכה - נותנין אותם מיד, ואע"פ שקיבל שכרה, נותן לו פגרא לכשתשבר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:2.english: Rent at the time of pulling - They give [the rent] immediately, and even though [the owner] received its rent, [the renter] gives him [payment for] the damage when it breaks.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:3.hebrew: אטו במנהגא תליא מילתא - היכי שבקינן להו לקבל שכר, הואיל וסופו לקנותה כולה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:3.english: Is that to say [that] this matter depends on custom - How do we allow them to receive rent, since in the end he is to buy all of it?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:4.hebrew: משום דמתניתא תניא - דמותר, כדקתני שלא עשאה דמים מחיים אלא לאחר מיתה, נהוג מנהגא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:4.english: Because the baraita taught - That it is permitted, as it teaches: "[because] he did not assess its monetary value while alive, only after death," they practiced [this] custom.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:5.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>, משום דמתניתא תניא מנהגא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:1:5.english: We read [the text as]: "Because the baraita taught [this, it is a] custom."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:2:1.english: After those who left them - After their father to the cemetery.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:2:2.hebrew: גופא דעובדא - שראית את מר שמואל נוהג כן, שהעדת זאת בשמו. הא ודאי פשיטא דלא שמעתא איתמר הכי בפירוש, אלא מכלל שראית אותו נוהג, העדת כן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:2:2.english: The actual incident - That you saw Mar Shmuel acting thus, [such] that you testified this in his name. For it is certainly obvious that [it] was not stated explicitly as a teaching; rather, from [the fact] that you saw him acting [thus], you testified so.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:1.english: [Regarding] that kettle - A cauldron, which they call caldiere [in Old French].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:2.english: Of the children of Mar Ukva - They were orphans.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:3.hebrew: תקיל ויהיב לה תקיל ושקיל לה - היה משכירה לאחרים, ושקלה כשהוא מוסרה להם, וחוזר ומקבלה במשקל. אם חסר נחושתה, משלמין לו דמי חסרונה, ויהיב ליה דמי אגר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:3.english: He would weigh it and give it [out], he would weigh it and take it [back] - He would rent it out to others, and weigh it when he handed it over to them, and receive it back by weight. If its copper was diminished, they would pay him the value of its loss and give him the rental fee.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:4.hebrew: פחתא - חסרון נחושתה. ואי ס"ד אסור להלוותן בריבית, אי אגרא — לא פחתא, למה נותנין שכר, הואיל ומקבלין עליהם השוכרין פחת נחושתה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:3:4.english: Depreciation - The loss of its copper. And if you should think [that] it is forbidden to lend [their property] on interest — "If [he takes] a rental fee, [he does] not [take] depreciation" — why do they pay a rental fee, since the renters accept upon themselves the depreciation of its copper?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:4:1.hebrew: בדיקנני - ביתומים גדולים שנתמלא זקנם ואינן קרוים יתומים, שרי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:4:1.english: For bearded ones - With older orphans whose beard has filled out and who are not called orphans, [it is] permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:4:2.hebrew: דהא מקבלי עלייהו חוסכא דנחשתא - פחת דמי הנחשת שנשאר, כדמפרש ואזיל דכל מה דמיקלי נחשא בצרי דמיה. אע"פ שמשלמין את חוסר המשקל, יש פחת בנחשת הנותר בו, הנשרף באור, וכל נחשת שרוף דמיו פחותים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:4:2.english: For they accept upon themselves the depreciation of the copper - [This refers to] the depreciation in value of the copper that remains, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain: that the more the copper is burned, the more its value is diminished. Even though [the renters] pay for the deficiency in weight, there is depreciation in the copper that remains in [the vessel], which is burned in the fire, and any burned copper has a diminished value.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:5:1.hebrew: קרוב לשכר - שהיו יתומים נוטלין חלק בשכר ואין נוטלין חלק בהפסד, אבל רבית ממש לא, אלא מה שישתכרו מעותיהם יחלוקו. ואע"ג דבדיקנני אסור, לאו רבית ממש הוא, אלא אבק רבית הוא ומדרבנן, וביתמי לא גזור, שלא יכלו מעותיהם להאכילם פרוטה אחר פרוטה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:5:1.english: Close to profit - That the orphans would take a share in the profit and not take a share in the loss, but actual interest — no; rather, whatever their money earns they divide. And even though for adults it is forbidden, it is not actual interest; rather, it is a semblance of interest and [prohibited] by rabbinic decree, and regarding orphans [the Sages] did not decree [it], so that their money should not be exhausted [by] feeding them perutah after perutah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:7:1.english: And we give them a zuz at a time - For their meals.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:8:1.hebrew: דהבא פריכא - גרוטאות של זהב, דודאי שלו הן ואינן פקדון, דלא עבידי אינשי דמפקדי דהבא פריכא בפקדון. וכיון דעשיר הוא ויש לו לגבות ממנו אם יאבדו מעותיו, יהבינן להו נהליה קרוב לשכר ורחוק להפסד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:8:1.english: Scraps of gold - Broken pieces of gold, for they are certainly his and are not a deposit, since people are not accustomed to deposit scraps of gold as a deposit. And since he is wealthy and there is [the wherewithal] to collect from him if his money is lost, we give them [the funds] to him close to profit and far from loss.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:9:1.hebrew: דמשפו ניכסיה - שנכסיו שקטין אצלו ואין ערעור על קרקעותיו. דמשפו כמו (ישעיהו י״ג:ב׳) על הר נשפה שאו נס, ומתרגמינן על טורא שליוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:9:1.english: Whose properties are quiet - For his properties are peaceful for him, and there is no challenge against his lands. [The word] demishpu is like (Isaiah 13:2): "Upon a quiet [nishpeh] mountain lift up a banner," and we translate [it in Aramaic]: "Upon a tranquil mountain."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:9:2.hebrew: בבי דינא - בפני ב"ד שיש להם כח להפקיר נכסי המקבל אצל היתומים, ולהתנות עמו קרוב לשכר ורחוק להפסד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 70a:9:2.english: In court - Before a court that has the power to declare the recipient's property ownerless in favor of the orphans, and to stipulate with him [terms that are] close to profit and far from loss.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:2:1.hebrew: מעות של יתומים מותר להלוותן ברבית - ה"מ למיפרך: תיפוק ליה משום לוה, דקעבר ב"לא תשיך" (דברים כג)! אלא דעדיפא פריך; א"נ, קסבר דלא מחייב לוה משום "לא תשיך" אלא כשגם המלוה מוזהר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:2:1.english: "Money belonging to orphans is permitted to lend with interest" - [The Gemara] could have asked: Let [the prohibition] be derived because of the borrower, who transgresses "You shall not pay interest" (Deuteronomy 23)! Rather, [Rav Naḥman] raises a stronger objection. Alternatively, he holds that the borrower is not liable for "You shall not pay interest" unless the lender is also prohibited [from taking interest].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:4:1.hebrew: דקא מקבלי עלייהו חוסכא דנחשא - משמע, אע"ג דקא מקבל נותן עליה זולא ויוקרא, הוה אסור משום דאחריות על המקבל — אף על גב דאחריות לא הויא אלא משעת שבירה — אלא דוקא משום פחת דחוסכא דנחשא שרי ליקח שכר. והא דשרי לעיל (בבא מציעא דף סט:) נמי בספינא אגרא ופגרא, היינו משום דמקבל עליה קלקול הספינה שמתקלקל העץ במים, דלא משלם למשכיר אלא מה שהיא משתברת. ומכאן קשה לפי' ריב"ן, שפירש לעיל שמותר ליתן עיסקא למחצית שכר קרוב לשכר ורחוק להפסד, כיון דמקבל נותן יוקרא וזולא; דא"כ, למה היה צריך כאן לקבל חוסכא דנחשא? לא יקבל אלא זולא! ועוד, דאמרינן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף סח:) "ותרי תילתי בהפסד ותילתא באגר" — למה ליה למיעבד הכי? ליקבל עליה הנותן זולא, ולישתרי אפילו יהא כל אחריות על המקבל! והא דאמרינן לעיל (בבא מציעא דף סד.) גבי חמרא "אי תקפה ברשותך", ומסקינן "כיון שמקבל עליה יוקרא וזולא קרוב לזה ולזה הוא" — התם שאני, דמכר גמור הוא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:4:1.english: "As they accept upon themselves the depreciation of the copper" - This implies that even though the giver accepts upon himself [fluctuations in] cheapness and expensiveness, it would [still] be forbidden because the responsibility [for loss] is upon the recipient — even though [that] responsibility is only from the time of breakage — rather, it is specifically because of the wear of the depreciation of the copper that it is permitted to take rent. And that which [the Gemara] permits above (Bava Metzia 69b) also regarding a ship, [taking both] rent and [compensation for] breakage, that is because [the lessor] accepts upon himself the deterioration of the ship, as the wood deteriorates in the water, so that [the lessee] only pays the lessor for what is broken. And from here there is a difficulty with the explanation of Rivan, who explained above that it is permitted to give an iska [investment partnership] for half the profit — [which is] near to profit and far from loss — since the investor accepts [fluctuations in] expensiveness and cheapness; for if so, why was it necessary here to accept the depreciation of the copper? Let him accept only cheapness! And furthermore, [regarding] that which we say above (Bava Metzia 68b), "and two-thirds in loss and one-third in profit" — why did he need to do this? Let the investor accept upon himself cheapness, and let it be permitted even if all responsibility is upon the recipient! And [as for] that which we say above (Bava Metzia 64a) regarding wine, "If it turns sour, it is in your possession," and we conclude, "Since he accepts upon himself [fluctuations in] expensiveness and cheapness, it is near to both this and that" — there it is different, because it is a complete sale.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:8:1.hebrew: אתא מריה ויהיב סימנא ושקיל - תימה: דהיכי שקיל ע"י סימנא? הא מצי האי למימר "לקוח הוא בידי"! ואי חיישינן דלמא מודה ליה מקבל דשלו הן, א"כ דהבא פריכא נמי ניחוש שמא מודה ליה! וא"ת: כיון דאין בו סימן, למה יאמינו לו? א"כ, בדבר מסוים נמי ניחוש שמא הגיד לו! ואפילו לא היה אמיד, היה נאמן לומר "לקוח הוא בידי", דאימור מציאה אשכח, או מתנה נתנו לו. והא דאמר בפ' האשה שלום (יבמות קטו: ושם ד"ה וכן) גבי שומשמי, דטוען נפקד "דידיה שקלתנהו והני אחריני נינהו", ואמרינן התם "אימור איתרמויי איתרמו" — דמשמע הא לא שכיח דמתרמי, דהוה חשיב סימנא מעליא והיה נאמן המפקיד להוציא מידו — התם היה לו למפקיד עדים שהפקיד בחבית במדה זו, ועדיין נמצאו כן בחבית. ואפילו לא היו עדים בדבר, היה נאמן אי הוה סימנא מעליא, כיון שהנפקד אינו טוען "לקוחין הן בידי" או "שלי היו מעולם, ובני ביתי הגידו לך הסימן", אלא מודה שהפקיד לו, אלא שאומר "כמו שאירע הסימן בשלך, כן אירע בשלי"; ואע"ג דאית ליה מגו, לא היה נאמן דהוי מגו במקום עדים. ונראה לפרש, דהכא חיישינן דלמא אתי מריה אחר מיתת המקבל, כדאמרי' בהכותב (כתובות פה: ושם ד"ה ועוד): "ועוד", גבי ההוא דאפקיד כסא דכספא בי חסא, שכיב חסא ולא פקיד, אתא מריה ויהיב סימנא, אר"נ: חדא דידעינן ביה בחסא דלא אמיד, ועוד דקא יהיב סימנא — משמע אפי' אמיד נמי, כיון דיהיב סימנא, שקיל! ומיהו קשה: כיון דאמיד הוא, אמאי לא נטעון ליתמי "לקוח הוא"? והיינו יכולין לומר דלא טענינן להו "לקוח" אלא בדברים שהיה אביהם משתמש בחייו, אבל דברים שלא היה משתמש בהם, דומה הוא שבפקדון הם אצלו, ומהדרינן בסימנא. אבל א"כ, לא שבקת חיי לכל בני עשירים, שאדם שהיה רגיל אצלם ויודע עניינם ילך ויגיד לאחרים דלא עיילי ונפקי בביתם סימני כסף וזהב שלהם! ועוד אכתי קשה: דלמה ליה הכא דאית ליה דהבא פריכא? אפילו דבר המסוים נמי, אלא שיאמר בפני ב"ד שהוא שלו! ונראה לפרש, דהכא בשמעתין חיישינן שמא יבאו עדים שהפקיד בידו חפץ שיש בו סימן זה, וכיון שמביא עדים, אין להם לב"ד למנוע מלהראות החפץ לעדים, ויכירו אם הוא זה. ובההיא דהכותב עיקר טעמא הוי משום דלא אמיד, וכיון דלא אמיד אין לנו לטעון ליתומים "לקוח ביד אביהן", דמציאה או מתנה מילתא דלא שכיח הוא, ולא טענינן ליתמי, אע"ג שאביהן היה נאמן לטעון "לקוח היה בידי". והכי פירושו: "חדא דידעינן ביה דלא אמיד" — ובטעם זה לחודיה סגי; "ועוד" — דאפילו את"ל דלא מהני אמיד לחודיה, הא קא יהיב סימנא, ויועילו שני הטעמים יחד. א"נ, מעיקרא לא ר"ל שהיה הטעם דלא אמיד לחודיה דיי, אלא מתחילה לא נתכוון לומר אלא שבין שניהם יועילו. והא דאמר בסוף פ"ק דכתובות (דף יג:) גבי ארוס וארוסתו, דאמר התם רב יוסף: "למאי ניחוש לה? חדא דקא מודה, ועוד האמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל הלכה כר"ג", ופריך: "ובהא כי לא מודה מי מכשר רבן גמליאל?" — התם לא מצי למימר שיועילו שני הטעמים, דאי טעמא ד"הא קא מודה" לא מהני לחודיה, לא מהני נמי בהדיה דהלכה כרבן גמליאל, כיון דלא מכשר אלא ברוב כשירין אצלה, והכא כולן פסולין אצלה לבד מארוס. ולהכי פריך "כי לא מודה", פי': כי לא מהני טעמא דמודה לחודיה, מי מהני בהדיה טעמא דהלכה כר"ג כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 70a:8:1.english: The owner will come and provide a distinguishing mark and take [it] - This is perplexing: how can he take [it] by means of a distinguishing mark? Surely this [recipient] can say, "It is purchased in my possession"! And if we are concerned that perhaps the recipient will admit to him that it is his — if so, [with] scraps of gold as well, let us be concerned that perhaps he will admit to him! And if you say: since there is no distinguishing mark on it, why would they believe him? If so, with a specific item as well, let us be concerned that perhaps he told him [the distinguishing mark]! And even if he were not wealthy, he would be believed to say, "It is purchased in my possession," for one can say he found a lost object or they gave [it] to him as a gift. And [as for] that which is stated in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah Shalom (Yevamot 115b, and ibid., s.v. VeKhen) regarding sesame seeds — where the bailee claims, "You took yours and these are different ones," and we say there, "Say that they happened to match," which implies that where it is not common to happen by coincidence, it would be considered a valid distinguishing mark and the depositor would be believed to extract [it] from his possession — there, the depositor had witnesses that he deposited [sesame seeds] in a barrel of this measure, and they were still found thus in the barrel. And even if there were no witnesses to the matter, he would be believed if there were a valid distinguishing mark, since the bailee is not claiming "they are purchased in my possession" or "they were always mine, and my household members told you the distinguishing mark," rather he admits that [the depositor] deposited with him, only he says, "Just as the distinguishing mark occurred in yours, so it occurred in mine"; and even though he has a migo [an alternative, stronger claim], he would not be believed, for it is a migo in the face of witnesses. And it appears [correct] to explain that here we are concerned that perhaps the owner will come after the death of the recipient, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaKotev (Ketubot 85b, and ibid., s.v. VeOd): "Furthermore," regarding that [person] who deposited a silver cup in the house of Chasa; Chasa died and did not leave instructions; the owner came and provided a distinguishing mark; Rav Nachman said: "Firstly, we know about Chasa that he is not wealthy, and furthermore, he provides a distinguishing mark" — which implies that even if he were wealthy as well, once he provides a distinguishing mark, he takes [it]! However, this is difficult: since he is wealthy, why should we not claim on behalf of the orphans, "It is purchased"? Now, we could say that we only claim "purchased" on their behalf for things that their father used during his lifetime, whereas things that he did not use, it is likely that they are [held] by him as a deposit, and we return [them] based on a distinguishing mark. However, if so, you have left no livelihood for all the children of wealthy people, for a person who was accustomed [to visit] them and knows their affairs will go and tell others who do not enter and exit their house the distinguishing marks of their silver and gold! And furthermore, it is still difficult: why does he need here [to look for someone] who has scraps of gold? Even a specific item as well [would work], provided that he declares before the court that it is his! Rather, it appears [correct] to explain that here in our passage we are concerned that perhaps witnesses will come [testifying] that [the owner] deposited in his hand an item that has this distinguishing mark; and once he brings witnesses, the court cannot refrain from showing the item to the witnesses, and they will recognize whether this is it. And in that [incident] in HaKotev, the primary reason was because he is not wealthy; and since he is not wealthy, we should not claim on behalf of the orphans that it was purchased in their father's possession, for finding a lost object or [receiving] a gift is an uncommon matter, and we do not claim [it] on behalf of orphans, even though their father would have been believed to claim "it was purchased in my possession." And this is its explanation: "Firstly, we know about him that he is not wealthy" — and this reason alone suffices; "and furthermore" — even if you were to say that [not being] wealthy alone does not suffice, behold he provides a distinguishing mark, and the two reasons together will suffice. Alternatively, originally he did not mean to say that the reason of "he is not wealthy" alone was sufficient; rather, from the outset he only intended to say that between the two of them they will suffice. And [as for] that which is stated at the end of the first chapter of Ketubot (13b) regarding a betrothed man and his betrothed, where Rav Yosef said there: "What should we be concerned about? Firstly, he admits [it], and furthermore, Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel that the halakhah follows Rabban Gamliel," and [the Gemara] asks: "And in this [case], when he does not admit [it], does Rabban Gamliel declare [her] fit?" — there, one cannot say that the two reasons together suffice, because if the reason of "behold he admits [it]" does not suffice on its own, [the reason] that the halakhah follows Rabban Gamliel does not suffice along with it either, since [Rabban Gamliel] only declares [her] fit where the majority [of men] are fit for her, whereas here all [men] are unfit for her except for the betrothed. And therefore [the Gemara] asks, "when he does not admit [it]," meaning: when the reason that he admits [it] does not suffice on its own, does the reason that the halakhah follows Rabban Gamliel suffice along with it, etc.?
